title: Short answers: On and Ei ole
summary: A short affirmative possession reply echoes On. A short negative possession reply is Ei ole. The question already tells us the owner and thing.
objectives: Confirm possession with On or deny it with Ei ole.
Recognise the pattern, then produce it with the supporting words shown.

sections.title: How the pattern works
paragraphs: A short affirmative possession reply echoes On. A short negative possession reply is Ei ole. The question already tells us the owner and thing.

On. and Kyllä, on. are both natural affirmative replies. Ei ole. and Ei, ei ole. are both natural negative replies. Choose the reply from the English meaning requested, rather than guessing whether the owner has the thing.
keyPoints: Short answers: On and Ei ole
Use one singular thing and the owner form shown by the prompt.

examples.english: Do I have a ball? — I do have it.
steps: minulla means “I as the owner”. The question names pallo (“a ball”).
The reply confirms possession, so echo fixed On (“have/has” here).
The short verb reply leaves the understood owner and thing unspoken; do not conjugate it for that owner.

examples.english: Do you have a book? — You do not have it.
steps: sinulla means “you as the owner” for one person. The question names kirja (“a book”).
The reply denies possession, so use fixed Ei ole (“do/does not have” here).
The short verb reply leaves the understood owner and thing unspoken; do not conjugate it for that owner.

examples.english: Does she have a dog? — She does have it.
steps: hänellä means “he as the owner” or “she as the owner”; this example uses “she”. The question names koira (“a dog”).
The reply confirms possession, so echo fixed On (“have/has” here).
Kyllä (“yes”) is an optional answer particle; On. alone also confirms possession.

examples.finnish: Onko meillä auto? — Ei, ei ole.
examples.english: Do we have a car? — We do not have it.
steps: meillä means “we as the owner”. The question names auto (“a car”).
The reply denies possession, so use fixed Ei ole (“do/does not have” here).
The first Ei (“no”) is an optional answer particle; Ei ole. alone also denies possession.

examples.english: Do you have a game? — You do have it.
steps: teillä means “you as the owner” for a group. The question names peli (“a game”).
The reply confirms possession, so echo fixed On (“have/has” here).
The short verb reply leaves the understood owner and thing unspoken; do not conjugate it for that owner.

examples.english: Do they have a pen? — They do not have it.
steps: heillä means “they as the owner”. The question names kynä (“a pen”).
The reply denies possession, so use fixed Ei ole (“do/does not have” here).
The short verb reply leaves the understood owner and thing unspoken; do not conjugate it for that owner.

examples.english: Do I have a cat? — I do have it.
steps: minulla means “I as the owner”. The question names kissa (“a cat”).
The reply confirms possession, so echo fixed On (“have/has” here).
Kyllä (“yes”) is an optional answer particle; On. alone also confirms possession.

examples.finnish: Onko meillä tyyny? — Ei, ei ole.
examples.english: Do we have a pillow? — We do not have it.
steps: meillä means “we as the owner”. The question names tyyny (“a pillow”).
The reply denies possession, so use fixed Ei ole (“do/does not have” here).
The first Ei (“no”) is an optional answer particle; Ei ole. alone also denies possession.

commonMistakes: A possession reply stays On or Ei ole, even with meillä or heillä; do not answer Olemme or Emme ole.
Answer the stated fact: On confirms possession and Ei ole denies it.
Kyllä can accompany an affirmative verb reply; an additional Ei can introduce a negative reply. Keep the verb reply when the task requests it.
